headline: Bill Gates attempts to install Windows Movie Maker
summary: The Microsoft co-founder was reportedly seen trying to install the legacy software on a new device.
details: In a surprising turn of events, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates was observed attempting to install Windows Movie Maker on a device.
The incident, reportedly witnessed by others, suggests a desire to use the older, now discontinued, video editing software.
Windows Movie Maker was a popular, albeit basic, video editing tool included with earlier versions of Windows.
It was officially retired by Microsoft in 2017, with support ending and downloads removed from official channels.

headline_marked: [[Bzip3]] offers better compression than BZip2, reaching 17MiB/s
headline: Bzip3 offers better compression than BZip2, reaching 17MiB/s
summary: A new compression tool, Bzip3, claims higher ratios and faster speeds than its predecessor, with benchmarks showing up to 17MiB/s on x64 Linux.
details: Bzip3 is presented as a spiritual successor to BZip2, aiming for superior compression ratios and enhanced performance. It achieves this through advanced techniques like an order-0 context mixing entropy coder, a fast Burrows-Wheeler transform using suffix arrays, and a RLE with Lempel Ziv+Prediction pass.

The tool is particularly effective at compressing text and code, similar to its predecessor. Benchmarks indicate that on x64 Linux with Clang 13, Bzip3 can achieve compression speeds of up to 17MiB/s and decompression speeds of 23MiB/s per thread.

The developer has released benchmarks comparing Bzip3 against other compressors like Turbo-Range-Coder and BSC. These tests involved compressing large archives of Perl 5 source code, demonstrating Bzip3's competitive performance in real-world scenarios.

It's important to note the developer's disclaimer: 'I TAKE NO RESPONSIBILITY FOR ANY LOSS OF DATA ARISING FROM THE USE OF THIS PROGRAM/LIBRARY, HOWSOEVER CAUSED.' While extensive testing has been done, the complexity of the algorithms means there's a small possibility of bugs.

Bzip3 is licensed under LGPLv3 only and is not dual-licensed. While performance can vary, x64 Linux builds with Clang 13 are generally the fastest, with Windows and 32-bit builds potentially being slower.
